lines: Have you ever heard a recording of your own voice and been surprised?
You may have thought, “Is that really my voice?”
Maybe your accent seems stronger in recordings, or your voice sounds higher than you expected.
When we speak, we hear our own voice in two ways.
First, we hear our voice like other sounds around us — through the air.
The sound travels through the air and into our ears.
But we also hear our voice in another way.
When we speak, our vocal cords shake, and this shaking makes a sound.
The sound goes through our bones and reaches our inner ears.
So our voice sounds lower and deeper to us but higher to other people.
body.text: Have you ever heard a recording of your own voice and been surprised? You may have thought, “Is that really my voice?” Maybe your accent seems stronger in recordings, or your voice sounds higher than you expected. Many people feel this way. The reason is quite simple. When we speak, we hear our own voice in two ways. First, we hear our voice like other sounds around us — through the air. The sound travels through the air and into our ears. But we also hear our voice in another way. When we speak, our vocal cords shake, and this shaking makes a sound. The sound goes through our bones and reaches our inner ears. This makes low sounds stronger. So our voice sounds lower and deeper to us but higher to other people.
